content: 1. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rifabutin by reducing its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Rifapentine also decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate via CYP3A4 induction. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Additionally, rilpivirine increases the risk of QTc prolongation when combined with erythromycin stearate. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. Monitor closely. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Additionally, erythromycin stearate increases rimegepant levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of riociguat by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose if necessary. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of risperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Ritonavir, in turn, increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients with renal impairment may experience significant increases in rivaroxaban exposure, leading to an elevated bleeding risk. Use rivaroxaban in this situation only if the potential benefit outweighs the risk. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of roflumilast by mechanisms involving dual inhibition of CYP3A4 and CYP1A2. Modify therapy or monitor closely, as this may increase systemic exposure and adverse reactions. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of roflumilast topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of romidepsin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin by mechanisms involving other pathways. Use caution and monitor closely. However, erythromycin stearate may also decrease rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 16. Rucaparib increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 17. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sacubitril/valsartan by mechanisms involving hepatic uptake transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. 20. Sarecycline increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for toxicities of P-glycoprotein substrates, which may require dosage reduction. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 23. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage and resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 25. Sertraline and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Sevoflurane and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider a starting dose of 25 mg in patients treated with erythromycin. 28. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of silodosin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to an increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. OATP1B1 inhibitors may further increase the risk of myopathy. 30. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. 31. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Sodium citrate/citric acid increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with antibiotics reduces efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed for drug activation. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, limit the duration of co-administration and monitor for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 37. Sorafenib and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Erythromycin stearate and sotalol both increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 39. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Regularly monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function if sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Stiripentol increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, requiring careful monitoring of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates. 43. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of streptomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sulbactam/durlobactam by mechanisms involving OATP1 inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 46. Sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of tacrolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 50. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. For daily use, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day, or for as-needed use, limit to 10 mg every 72 hours. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with P-glycoprotein inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. 52. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibition reduces the metabolism of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. 53. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. 54. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, erythromycin stearate increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose.
